title: Unstick escape-duct and telemetry anchors — personal scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
A compact personal checklist / scratchpad for emergency 'unstick' ops during a bad rollout. Intended for quick decision-making when a canary/rollout is not progressing or is actively harming user experience. Not a runbook replacement — this is my hand-rolled, prioritized notes for fast action and telemetry sanity checks.

Context notes (why I keep this short):
- Lots of quiet-rollout docs exist; this is intentionally terse and action-first.
- Targets mostly model flips (hosted & dedicated) but includes tenant pin escapes.
- I assume I have access to the console, admin tokens, and a single SRE on call.

Quick decision flow (5 steps, 2-minute triage):
1) Observe: check latency P95, error rate, model-contract-failures, and user complaints channel.
2) Stop bleed: divert 100% new sessions to previous stable model variant if the rollback path exists. If not, pin traffic at 0% for the suspect variant.
3) Stabilize infra: throttle batching, reduce max concurrency for problematic workers, and escalate to SRE if GPU OOM or node crash observed.
4) Capture artifacts: capture a 10-minute trace snapshot, sample 50 failing requests, and export KV cache stats (cache hit/miss by tenant).
5) Reintroduce slowly: runway test with 0.5–1% cohort, observe for 30 minutes with short SLO windows.

Commands and quick console actions I rely on:
- Redirect traffic (console): Route > model-rollouts > select rollout > set weight previous=99 current=1 > apply.
- API pin (example): curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://console.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/pin -d '{\"model\":\"m-v2.1\",\"weight\":0}'
- Telemetry snapshot: rwdctl trace capture --duration 10m --filter 'model:m-v2.1' --out /tmp/unstick-trace.json
- Cache export: rwdctl kvstats export --model m-v2.1 --tenants 50 --out /tmp/kvstats.csv
- Emergency disable (if routing broken): rwdctl model disable --model m-v2.1 --reason 'unstick emergency'

Telemetry anchors (what I watch right away):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for tokens-per-second and total response time. Look for a sudden P95 climb > 2x baseline.
- Errors: 5xx, model-contract (schema/parse) errors, hallucination-rate signals from eval hooks.
- Throughput drop: client retries causing thundering behavior — watch request rate + retry rate.
- Resource signals: GPU mem pressure, OOMs, process restarts, queue depth.
- Cost-safety: runaway token generation (looping prompts) — tokens/s spiking.

Threshold heuristics I use (not formal SLOs):
- If P95 > 2x baseline OR 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase in 10m -> immediate diversion.
- If GPU OOMs > 1 crash in 5 minutes -> scale down concurrency and pin.
- If tenant-specific error burst (single tenant > 10x normal) -> isolate tenant and pin for that tenant only.

Pinning patterns (how I pick the pin):
- Preferred: pin to last-stable commit-model (immutable artifact ID) rather than 'previous' floating alias.
- Tenant pin: prefer SDK flag toggle per-tenant before global pin if problem appears localized.
- Partial pin example: set model:m-v2.1 weight=0 for tenant:acme, keep global weight unchanged.

Warmup & reintroduce checklist (after emergency):
- Verify previous stable model passes canonical smoke prompts (5 prompts covering critical flows).
- Clear KV prefix caches only if cache corruption suspected; avoid full cache flush during high load.
- Replay sampled failing requests against the pinned model offline; document differences.
- Gradual re-enable: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% -> 15% over monitoring windows (30m/30m/1h/2h). Adjust cadence if errors reappear.

Observation panel (what to open immediately):
- Rollouts page (live weights)
- Model metrics: latency/error/cost per token
- Traces: top 20 traces with highest latencies
- Logs: aggregator for model-worker stderr (OOM stack traces)
- Customer ops channel thread + watch for reproducer snippets

Owner notes and mental model tips:
- Keep 'escape duct' as the path that minimizes user impact (tenant pinning preferred).
- Minimize global state changes: prefer targeted pins, then region-level, then global.
- If the issue is quality (not infra), prefer model ratio reduction (route most requests to stable) not immediate disable; preserves auth and integration stability.
- Document every step in the incident thread with timestamps and actor names.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for me to tidy into a formal runbook):
- Add a tiny autotest that runs 200 synthetic prompts through the pinned model for quick canary validation.
- Define clear API contract for tenant-scoped pin (currently partial and sometimes manual).
- Create an automated telemetry alert that triggers the 'stop bleed' diversion when thresholds met (needs coord with observability).

Post-incident notes template (copy into incident doc after the fact):
- Time window of adulteration (start/end)
- Primary metric that triggered -> value before, during, after
- Quick root cause guess (model, infra, dataset)
- Artifacts captured (trace, sample requests, kv dump) + location
- Recovery steps taken and timeframe
- Follow-ups / owners assigned

Quick heuristics I scribbled when tired during a midnight incident:
- Always capture before you change; quick snapshot > nothing.
- If in doubt route to stable alias, not to 'disable' unless infra catastrophic.
- Tenant pinning is your friend; treat global changes as last resort.

End of scratchpad.

(Notes for myself: turn into a short runbook card; add links to specific console actions & automate the common curl flows into an internal CLI wrapper.)
